Thanks Naomi — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: for PHI we have a mix of state-level minima (e.g., CA) and contractual obligations; our default for treatment records is 7 years unless otherwise agreed. Will Redwood support per-tenant retention policies?
- Audit logging: we need immutable, tamper-evident logs for access to PHI with a 3-year retention and the ability to export on request. Are logs stored encrypted with customer-controlled keys?
- SOC2: we attached a short list of items we’ll need (see verity_security_questions.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an encrypted audit trail export to Verity’s S3?

If you can respond with specific constraints (especially around KV cache and whether PHI can be kept out of any cached state), we can assign internal owners. I’m tentatively assigning Samira to lead the IT Sec coordination.

Alex

Naomi — posted a technical draft below you can copy into the MAP. Quick notes first: we can support per-tenant retention via policy tags at the routing layer; audit logs are append-only and stored encrypted (customer KMS supported) and we can export a gzipped JSONL bundle to S3. KV cache: default behavior is to cache model context to speed up repeat requests; we can turn on PHI-safe mode (no KV cache writes) per-route if they require it.

Draft for MAP (technical language):
- Retention capabilities: Redwood supports configurable per-tenant retention windows via the routing policy. Retention windows are enforced at persistence and are immutable once committed; recommended default for PHI subsets is 7 years. Exceptions require a written retention override from Verity legal.
- Audit logging & exports: All access to request/response records that touch PHI is logged in an append-only audit trail. Logs are encrypted in transit and at rest; customers may supply a KMS key to manage encryption. Exports: Redwood can produce a tamper-evident JSONL export (gzipped) and deliver to a customer-owned S3 bucket with TLS. Retention of logs is configurable (min 90 days, recommended 3 years for PHI).
- KV cache / PHI handling: We recommend redacting PHI at the app layer prior to sending. If Verity requires that PHI be processed in cleartext for feature purposes, Redwood offers a PHI-safe runtime mode that disables KV cache writes and pins ephemeral memory to avoid persistence.
- Dependencies: Customer S3 bucket + write ACL for exports; KMS key ARN if customer-managed keys required; Signed non-disclosure for access to any internal pen test artifacts.

Attachments: I started a cleaned MAP draft (redwood_map_draft.docx) with timelines and owners filled. Looked at the suggested targets and bumped one week for engineering slack.

If Rachel flags anything contract-wise I’ll adjust.

—Marissa
